title: Noor and the Orchard
premise: Casper Nakamura, a wedding planner who swore off love after his own engagement collapsed, is hired to orchestrate a farewell party at a dying orchard estate on an island ferry route. A freak snowstorm strands him with Noor Haddad, the estate's estranged heir — and the woman who was once his best friend, business partner, and the one who walked away with their shared company and his heart. Trapped together as the orchard's fate hangs on a contested will, they must untangle a decade-old betrayal involving a forged signature, a loyal grandmother's silence, and the truth of who really stole what from whom. Forgiving each other proves easier than forgiving themselves; the story ends with them choosing to rebuild the orchard together, boarding the last ferry not to leave but to bring back the people they need.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former estate lawyer turned novelist who grew up among family orchards in the Pacific Northwest. Their fiction explores how inheritance — of land, guilt, and love — shapes the stories we tell ourselves.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Three years after losing everything, Casper plans flawless weddings for strangers while refusing his own invitations to feel anything. A lucrative commission arrives: a farewell gala at Meridian Orchard, owned by a client he's never met. Beat: controlled numbness cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wouldn't Give a Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The contract is signed through lawyers; the orchard's owner remains anonymous. His assistant notices the return address matches a town Casper avoids mentioning. He takes the job anyway, telling himself it's just money. Beat: denial dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Ferry to Meridian
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor Haddad returns to the island she fled ten years ago to settle her grandmother Sitti Rose's estate before selling it to developers. She finds the orchard half-abandoned, the trees still bearing fruit no one harvests. Beat: grief arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: Snowfall at the Dock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The last ferry of the season departs early as a storm closes in, stranding latecomers. Casper arrives for the venue walkthrough; Noor arrives to sign sale papers. They recognize each other across the empty dock. Beat: the past walking toward them in wet wool coats.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Forced to share the farmhouse, they trade barbed civility. Flashback threads reveal they built a wedding company together at twenty-three — until Noor sold it out from under him and vanished. Beat: old wounds reopening with surgical precision.

chapters.title: Sitti Rose's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In her grandmother's untouched kitchen, Noor finds a sealed letter addressed to 'whoever still believes in this place' — and a second will draft that contradicts the one her lawyer holds. Beat: suspicion that the betrayal she remembers may have had another author.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. With roads buried, they negotiate truce rules: he'll stage the farewell gala anyway (the client insists), she'll let him, and neither asks about the past. Both break the rule within a day. Beat: proximity defeating pride.

chapters.title: The Gala That Was Never Ordered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor discovers the anonymous client's instructions are oddly specific — a menu her grandmother loved, songs from her parents' wedding. Someone wanted this party. She begins to wonder if the sale itself was orchestrated. Beat: unease blooming into investigation.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Working side by side to clear storm damage, they fall into old rhythms — banter, shared coffee, finishing each other's checklists. Casper catches himself laughing and hates how easy it is. Beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Comparing documents, Noor finds her signature on a transfer she never signed — dated during the week her father died, when she was unreachable. The original company sale that ruined Casper bears the same forgery pattern. Beat: horror reframing history.

chapters.title: What I Thought You Did
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating scenes. Over whiskey, they finally tell each other their versions of the breakup — and realize both were fed lies by the same person: Uncle Marwan, the estate's trusted manager. Beat: devastating mutual reckoning.

chapters.title: Marwan's Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Searching the estate office, they find Marwan's hidden ledger: years of skimming orchard profits, forged papers, and a plan to flip the land cheap. But one entry stops them cold — payments made to someone close to Casper. Beat: rising tension, new suspicion.

chapters.title: The Loyal One
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The payments went to Casper's former fiancée, Elena — now Marwan's business partner. Noor confronts the question she fears most: did Casper know? Meanwhile Casper, reading the ledger alone, reaches the same page. Beat: loyalty versus truth at its sharpest.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cold Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Accusations flare; Casper admits Elena asked him about the orchard months ago and he said nothing, ashamed of his own lingering ties. Noor admits she almost sold without reading the will out of spite. Beat: honesty as both wound and salve.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Kiss
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. After the fight, exhausted and stripped bare, they admit the truth under the truth: they never stopped loving each other, only trusting. A kiss in the frost-killed apple rows. Beat: surrender without resolution.

chapters.title: Elena Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Roads partially clear; Elena lands unannounced with Marwan, pressing Noor to sign before the will contest deadline. Smooth, plausible, poisonous. Casper plays host while secretly photographing documents. Beat: the trap tightening.

chapters.title: The Farewell Gala
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The gala happens — beautiful, bittersweet, full of islanders who share memories that corroborate the ledger. Mid-toast, Marwan announces the sale is final. Casper publicly reveals the forged signature. Beat: climax igniting.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Lawyers are days away; Marwan moves to burn the evidence in the estate office fire. Noor and Casper, with the islanders' help, save the ledger and corner Marwan with testimony, recordings, and the community as witness. Beat: climax — truth enforced by loyalty, not courts.

chapters.title: Confessions and Consequences
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marwan and Elena are exposed; the real will surfaces, leaving the orchard jointly to Noor and, surprisingly, a bequest to Casper — Sitti Rose knew more than anyone guessed. They sit with what forgiveness costs. Beat: aftermath, quiet and raw.

chapters.title: What We Rebuild
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Sale voided, debts settled, the orchard survives but barely. Noor offers Casper partnership — not in weddings, but in turning the orchard into a place where broken things grow back. He hesitates, terrified of repeating history. Beat: choice framed honestly.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Each writes the letter they owe themselves — Noor to the girl who fled, Casper to the man who stopped believing. They read them aloud in the kitchen, then burn them in the stove like Sitti Rose would have. Beat: emotional resolution, self-forgiveness achieved.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. On the dock, the final ferry waits. Instead of boarding away, they wave it off and walk back up the hill together, sending the boat to fetch family, workers, and a future. Spring buds on the first trees. Beat: hopeful, earned ending.
